title: NEET Counselling: AIQ vs State Quota, What Actually Changes
description: All India Quota and State Quota aren't just two names for the same process. They're run by different bodies, follow different eligibility rules, and (the part most students get wrong) you can apply to both.
author: Studyloaf Team

content.body: Clearing NEET is the first hurdle. What happens after (the counselling process that actually turns your score into a seat) runs on a system most students only start learning about after results are out, which is exactly the wrong time to be learning it. Here's the part that trips people up most: AIQ and State Quota aren't two versions of the same process. They're genuinely different, run by different authorities.

content.heading: Who runs which quota
content.body: All India Quota (AIQ) seats (15% of the total) are counselled centrally by the Medical Counselling Committee (MCC), the same body regardless of which state you're from. State Quota seats (the remaining 85%) are counselled separately by each state's own authority, following that state's own rules.

content.heading: Why AIQ tends to be more competitive
content.body: AIQ pools candidates from the entire country into a single national merit list competing for a comparatively small slice of total seats. State Quota, by contrast, is usually restricted to candidates who meet that state's domicile requirement, which narrows the competing pool to a more local one. That's the main structural reason AIQ cutoffs tend to run higher than the equivalent state's own cutoff. Not because AIQ seats are somehow better, but because more people nationally are competing for fewer of them.

content.heading: The part students consistently get wrong
content.body: A genuinely common misconception: that participating in one counselling process locks you out of the other, or that accepting a state quota seat forfeits your AIQ eligibility somehow. If you meet the eligibility criteria for both, you can apply to both. MCC's process and your state's process run independently, and your standing in one doesn't affect or get reported to the other. Plenty of students run both tracks simultaneously and take whichever seat comes through with a better fit.

content.heading: What to actually check for your specific state
content.body: Domicile requirements, reservation categories, and the exact percentage split can vary by state: some states run additional quota categories beyond the basic AIQ/State split (management quota, NRI quota, minority institution quotas, depending on the state). The AIQ process itself is uniform nationally since MCC runs it the same way for everyone, but your state's specific counselling rules are worth reading directly from that state's official counselling authority rather than assuming they match a neighboring state's process.
